# dsh-settings-sync

Back up and restore **every** DeepSeek Harness setting through a private Git
repository you own — pr

ofile configuration, per-plugin settings, skills,
installed plugins, and MCP servers. Push from one

machine, restore on another,
with a restore point written before anything is overwritten.
中文说明
## Why this exists
DSH keeps its configuration in a few places, and they are all easy to lose:
| What | Where |

| The plugin inventory and the profile's bundle list | `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json` |
|
Per-plugin configuration (models, MCP servers, panel settings) | `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.p

atch.yml` |
| Skills | `~/.dsh/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/` |
| Per-plugin state (starred items, de
fault projects, tasks) | `~/.dsh/<plugin>/` |

`dsh export` copies that once, to a file you then have to move around yourself.
This plugin makes it

continuous: one private repository, one button in each
direction, and a diff you can read before yo

ivate repository, one button in each
direction, and a diff you can read before you commit to either.
## What gets synced
[代码示例省略，未执行]
And what deliberately does **not**:

- **Credentials.** `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, `tencent-intranet-auth.json`,
`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.tok

en`, `pairing.json` — excluded by name *and* by content.
On top of that, live values that appear ins

ide otherwise-synced config — an
`apiKey:` line in `cordis.patch.yml`, say — are replaced with
`<red

acted by dsh-settings-sync>` before the snapshot leaves the machine. The
configuration's *shape* is

preserved, so restoring still tells you a key
belongs there; you just fill it in again.

Redaction is **one-way**. A pull never writes the placeholder over a real local
value: the restorer

matches credential lines by key name and keeps the machine's
own secret, so restoring on the machine

the snapshot came from leaves its API
keys working. Only a machine that has no value yet receives t

he placeholder,
where it is exactly the right message — "a key is owed here".
- **Dependencies and c

aches.** `node_modules`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `__pycache__`,
`.plugin-manager` logs, attachment blobs.

- **Sessions and history.** `~/.dsh/sessions`, `~/.dsh/storages` — history is not
a setting, and it

is by far the largest thing in a DSH home.
- **Backups of previous edits.** Anything matching `.bak`

rgest thing in a DSH home.
- **Backups of previous edits.** Anything matching `.bak` in the profile.

A real machine — 21 installed plugins, 66 skills, six per-plugin state
directories — collects to **2
63 files and 1.4 MB**.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then, in DSH, either use **Settings → Plugins → Install**, or from a terminal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin adds a **Settings Sync** page under **Settings**, and on first launch
asks one question:
pull the remote settings down, or push these ones up.

Requirements: `git` on `PATH` (or set its absolute path in the plugin config),
and — only if you wan

t the one-click "create repository" button — the
GitHub CLI logged in with `gh auth login`.
## Use

1. **Set a repository.** Paste the URL of an empty private repository
(`git@github.com:you/dsh-setti

ngs.git` and
`https://github.com/you/dsh-settings.git` both work), or press
**Create private repo**

to have `gh` make one.
2. **Push** to upload this machine's settings.
3. On the other machine, insta
ll the plugin, paste the same URL, and **Pull**.

The diff panel shows exactly what a push would change — `+added`, `~modified`,
`-removed` — before y

ws exactly what a push would change — `+added`, `~modified`,
`-removed` — before you press anything.
### Automatic sync
| Setting | Meaning |

| **Redact secrets** | Replace live keys with a placeholder before upload. On by default. |
| **Auto

push** | Push after a settings change, on the check interval. |
| **Remote policy** | `never` — ign
ore the remote; `ask` — offer a choice (default); `always` — pull when the remote is ahead and local

is clean. |
| **Check interval** | Off, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, or 1 hour. |
### Safety model

- **Nothing is overwritten without a restore point.** Pull writes a full copy of
the current state u

nder `<stateDir>/backups/<timestamp>-snapshot/` first, and
that path is reported when the pull finis

hes. The restore points are listed on
the settings page and can be restored in one click.
- **A push

that collects nothing is refused.** A mis-resolved `HOME` looks like
"the user deleted everything",

and silently replacing a good backup with an
empty snapshot is unrecoverable. The same guard refuse

s a push that would
delete most of the tracked files unless you explicitly force it.
- **The snapsho

t is a real Git repository**, in `<stateDir>/mirror`. History is
the backup: `git log` in there show

s every sync, and `git show <commit>:profile/cordis.patch.yml`
gets you any earlier file. That is al

so why this plugin never needs its own
format for undo.
Everything lives under `$DSH_HOME/settings-sync` by default:

## Toolchain
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The tests run the real code against the real `git` binary and a scratch home
directory with a fake p

rofile, two skill roots, a per-plugin state directory, a
credential that must not be synced, and a b

are repository standing in for the
remote. Nothing about git is mocked, because git is the part most

likely to be
wrong.
## Design notes

**The mirror is a clone, not a database.** Keeping the snapshot as a normal
repository means the ent

ire undo mechanism is "check out an earlier commit", the
diff is `git status`, and the user can insp

ect or repair a sync from a terminal
without this plugin's help.

**Push and pull are serialized.** One operation at a time, one `busy` flag. A
second click waits rat

her than interleaving, and an automatic timer that fires
mid-pull is skipped.

**Authentication is the user's own.** Nothing in this plugin stores a token: it
runs the same `git`

the user runs, so osxkeychain, an SSH agent, or a
`credential.helper` applies unchanged. The corolla

ry is honest — if `git push`
